findings.finding: Found aₙ = Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁ (ratio of Fibonacci numbers). For even n, a₂ₙ → φ³ = 2+√5. So p=2,q=5. Compute 2^{5²}=2^{25}=33554432; 33554432 mod 99991 = 57447. (Key: geometry yields aₙ=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁).

Use normalized BC=1, BD=Fₙ/Fₙ₊₂, CD=Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ₊₂. Let sides b=CD+u, c=BD+u (u>0). Compute geometry (A, I, E, F, K, N). Cyclic K‑N‑K'‑B ⇒ u solves diff=0. Ratio = (CT·NB)/(BT·NE)=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. Hence aₙ=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁ → α=lim a₂ₙ=φ³=2+√5. p=2,q=5 → 2²⁵ mod 99991=57447. Pitfall: ignore spurious tiny‑u roots (degenerate AEF).

We set BC on x‑axis: B(0,0), C=a=Fₙ+Fₙ₊₁, D=(Fₙ,0). Let AB=c, AC=b=c+Fₙ₊₁−Fₙ. Coordinates: A(xA,yA) with xA=(c²−b²+a²)/(2a), yA=√(c²−xA²). Incircle I=(Fₙ,r), r=√((c−Fₙ)FₙFₙ₊₁/(c+Fₙ₊₁)). Tangency points: F=(Fₙ·A/c), E=C+(A−C)·Fₙ₊₁/b. N=proj_D onto EF. K=second intersection of circles (ABC) and (AEF). K′=reflection of K across EF. Cyclic B,N,K,K′ ⇔ circumcenter O of ΔBNK lies on EF ⇒ O is intersection of EF with perp‑bisector of BN; solve O·B=O·N. This yields a single c solving det=0. Using numeric bisection we find c_root and ratio R=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE). R simplifies to Fₙ₊₂/(Fₙ₊₁−Fₙ)=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. Hence aₙ=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. For even n, a_{2n}=F_{2n+2}/F_{2n−1}→φ³≈4.23607. So α=φ³= (1+√5)³/8 = (7+3√5)/2 = p+√q with p=7/2, q=45/4. Compute ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. (Finish arithmetic.)

Use normalized BC=1, BD=Fₙ/Fₙ₊₂, CD=Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ₊₂. Let sides b=CD+u, c=BD+u. Solve cyclic condition K,N,K′,B ⇒ u solves F_{n+2}/F_{n-1}=ratio. Hence aₙ=F_{n+2}/F_{n-1}→α=φ³=2+√5. Compute 2^{5²} mod 99991=57447. Pitfall: ignore degenerate u≈0 roots.
